messages:
sasha: Hey team — customer hit repeated 413s when sending large embedding batches to /v1/embeddings. They say it worked earlier but now fails for >8MB payloads. Request ID: req_78a2. Any ideas?

mike: 413 = Request Entity Too Large. Which client are they using? Node or curl? Also which model/dimension?

sasha: They said node SDK (v2.3.1) and sending an array of 25k small texts. Using model `embed-large-1536`. Each embedding request is a big JSON of objects.

elena: 25k is a lot. Our API has a default request body soft limit (payload size) ~8MB per request for the hosted gateway, plus backend per-request processing limits. If they pack everything into one request it's expected to hit 413. Recommend chunking.

jon: Also check dimension mismatch logs — saw similar thread where customer got downstream `dimension mismatch` errors after naive chunking. They were concatenating partial vectors client-side. Are they attempting any client-side streaming assembly?

sasha: Customer says they tried splitting into chunks of 5k but then got some responses with `vector length 768 != 1536` for a subset. They didn't change model.

mike: That screams mixed-model routing or a middle proxy truncating JSON. Could also be double-encoding (base64) or a serialization bug in their splitter. Need repro steps.

sasha: I've asked for a minimal repro. They sent curl example:```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"embed-large-1536","input": ["text1","text2", ... 25000 items]}'``` They said splitting into 5k lists sometimes works but inconsistent.

elena: Two things to triage: 1) Ensure the model in the request is consistent and not being rewritten by a proxy. 2) Check if any of their items include binary or very long strings (like file dumps) that push per-item size up.

embed-prod-bot: [ingest] request=req_78a2 route=gateway-03 status=413 size=9431207 region=us-west1

jon: From prod logs: found a few gateway instances that had older model-mapping configs that would rewrite `embed-large-1536` to a legacy `embed-small-768` when under load. That would produce the exact dimension mismatch. Ops is rolling a config fix.

mike: Good catch. For the 413s though, we should recommend streaming/chunked upload patterns: - limit JSON payload < 6MB for safe margin - send arrays of ~500-2000 items depending on average text length - use concurrency across multiple connections if they need high throughput

elena: Add to that: show them how to implement chunking and resume semantics. Example Node pseudo-code:```js
async function sendBatches(items, batchSize=1000){
  for(let i=0;i<items.length;i+=batchSize){
    const chunk = items.slice(i,i+batchSize);
    await fetch('/v1/embeddings',{method:'POST',headers,body:JSON.stringify({model:'embed-large-1536',input:chunk})});
  }
}
``` Mention exponential backoff on 429/502 and retry-idempotency keys.

sasha: Customer asks about streaming (chunked transfer-encoding) so they don't build huge in-memory payloads. Do we support chunked encoding for embeddings?

elena: Our gateway accepts chunked transfer-encoding for streaming responses on completions, but for embeddings the canonical approach is multiple POSTs. However we have a multipart streaming ingest feature for enterprise (private) customers — needs special header `X-Embed-Stream: true` and part boundaries. Not enabled by default for hosted.

mike: So recommended immediate action: 1) Advise them to implement client-side chunking (500-2k items) 2) Expose parallel workers with limited concurrency (eg 4-8) 3) Provide a small repro script for us to validate 4) We'll confirm gateway config roll and check for any live rewrites that would cause dim mismatch

jon: Also capture these in their repro: include the raw request body size, `Content-Length` header, and the X-Request-ID if available. If they can reproduce 413 we need the gateway logs (we already have req_78a2 but more samples help).

sasha: I drafted an email with step-by-step repro + example chunker (Node + curl) and asked them to run and paste first failing request. Sent it now.

embed-prod-bot: [deploy] config-rollout started for gateway model-mapping (corr:deploy_993)

elena: After config rollout, if they still see dimension mismatch, request they capture one failing response body and a matching request — we can compare model field, headers, and any intermediate proxies.

mike: For long-term, doc we should add: embedding best practices -> chunking examples, target request sizes, parallelism patterns, and a note about private streaming ingest with `X-Embed-Stream`. I'll draft a short doc and link to support.

sasha: Great. I'll keep this thread updated with the customer's repro. Thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: follow-up: if customer needs near-real-time throughput for millions of items, recommend Dedicated/Private with multipart streaming enabled and local batching to avoid gateway limits.

sasha: update: customer ran our chunker -> no 413s so far, but they hit slower throughput since they ran with batchSize=500. We'll suggest tuning batch size by measuring average tokens per item and trying 1000/2000. Closing loop soon.
